cards.title: Bullet points: lead with product name + benefits, not features
cards.summary: Structure Amazon bullet points so the primary keyword appears first and each bullet translates a feature into a concrete customer outcome.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting the five bullet points on an Amazon listing (PDP copy) for a consumable or any private-label product.
steps: Make the exact primary keyword (e.g. 'Berberine Tea') the first two words of bullet one so Amazon reinforces what the product is.
Put the strongest quantified/emotional hook early — the source likes a number like '100% natural and organic' because specifics feel credible.

Convert every feature into the benefit the buyer actually experiences. Instead of 'supports healthy blood sugar levels,' describe outcomes like steady energy, easier weight maintenance, or eating sweets without a blood-sugar spike.
Note the trade-off: 'blood sugar support' can still be a valid keyword because many shoppers search it, so keep searchable phrasing where demand exists even if the literal benefit is more abstract.
Drop generic phrases no one searches (e.g. 'antioxidant-rich blend') and replace them with keywords people actually type.
Add sourcing specifics only if verifiable (e.g. 'sourced from the Himalayas') — verify before claiming.
Make the final bullet a 100% money-back guarantee. The source notes every Amazon product already carries this, but stating it explicitly reassures buyers.
Enter each bullet one at a time via 'add more' in Seller Central; the source's formula is copyable but keywords should be tailored to your product.
caveats: The bullet formula is the presenter's opinion, not a platform rule.
Keyword choice should follow actual search demand for your niche, verified with a keyword tool.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Make the main image differentiate on the search results grid
cards.summary: Winning the click depends on packaging and main-image choices that stand out against competitors' thumbnails on Amazon search.
cards.use_when: Designing product packaging and the main listing image before launch so the product is clickable in search results.
steps: Search your main keyword and screenshot the results grid to study what competitors' thumbnails look like (common palettes: whites, pale pinks, yellows).
Choose packaging colours that contrast with Amazon's white background — the source cites black packaging with red lettering for a high-caffeine tea to pop against boring competitor images.
Print the exact search term in large letters on the front of the packaging (e.g. 'High Caffeine Tea' / 'Berberine Tea') so shoppers instantly recognize a match.
Use a clean main image showing just the front of the packaging, and upload it via the listing's upload button.
Treat the main image as the highest-leverage listing asset: the source argues a weak image can kill a product before launch.
Verify current Amazon main-image requirements (pure white background, no text overlays on the photo itself) since the packaging text is printed, not overlaid.
caveats: The presenter's claim that the standout image is also the bestseller is an observation of one niche, not proof of causation.
Amazon main-image rules change; confirm current requirements in Seller Central.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use all eight side images to sell what buyers can't touch
cards.summary: Supplementary images substitute for the physical product experience and should include a comparison chart against competitors.
cards.use_when: Building the image gallery and A+ assets for an Amazon product page before or after launch.
steps: Upload as many of the eight available side images as possible — buyers can't hold the product, so images do the selling.
Include at least one graph or comparison chart showing how your product beats competitors.
Show lifestyle/usage, dimensions, ingredients or specs, and any guarantee details across the gallery.
Avoid low-quality photos: the source cites a seller (Mina) whose poor launch images cost over $10,000 in lost potential customers — treat as an illustrative example, not a benchmark.
Consider supplementing the gallery with A+ content (richer modules Amazon may suggest under Growth), since the source reports Amazon flagging potential sales lift from improved A+ content.
caveats: A+ content requires Brand Registry and may not be available to every seller.
The $10,000 figure is a single anecdote.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Fill product details thoroughly and consistently
cards.summary: Completing Amazon's product-detail attributes accurately (manufacturer, unit count, ingredients, expiration) prevents listing errors and improves discoverability.
cards.use_when: Creating a new Amazon listing and filling out the product-details section for a consumable or physical good.
steps: Manufacturer: you can enter your brand name or yourself even if a different factory makes the product.
Number of items = identical units per sale (one 30-teabag pouch = 1), not the count of tea bags inside.
Special ingredients: add distinctive actives (e.g. 'berberine') even if they're not in Amazon's dropdown.
Heat sensitivity and temperature rating: set for your product (frozen/chocolate goods are heat sensitive; tea is ambient room temperature).
Ingredients/caffeine/form factor/unit form: describe accurately (form factor = physical size/shape; unit form = teabags).
Unit count: enter how Amazon should measure value (e.g. 30 tea bags, or ounces for liquids) — this feeds value comparisons.

Expireable: yes for consumables (legally requires a date), no for shelf-stable paper/cardboard goods like the source's 'cocktail cards'. Set shelf life in days (365 for ~1 year; the source's tea may run 700+).
SKU is an internal code only you see — use something descriptive like 'berberine-tea-30count' rather than a bare name.
Quantity and condition matter mainly for FBM/used goods; new FBA sellers set condition = new.
caveats: Amazon's prompted questions vary by product category and change over time — verify the current fields.
The source notes its own first SKU choice was suboptimal, so pick descriptive SKUs from the start.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Price at 3x cost and position premium, not cheapest
cards.summary: The source recommends a minimum 3x markup over unit cost and pricing above competitors to signal quality and protect margin.
cards.use_when: Setting the launch price for a private-label Amazon product after calculating FBA fees.
steps: Use a floor of 3x your per-unit manufacturing cost (a $10 unit cost → list at $30 minimum) because Amazon fees typically consume about a third of the sale price.
Note the fee share isn't always a third: for a light $100 item it may be closer to 20–25%, so recalculate for your size/weight.
Factor in the 15% referral fee plus FBA pick-and-pack when checking margin.
Look at comparable products' price points and consider pricing slightly above competitors rather than undercutting — the source argues many shoppers want the best product, not the cheapest.
Position as a premium 'passion product' where the category supports it; the source set $28.99 for the example tea.
Set list price separately as the reference/retail price.
caveats: This is the presenter's stated preference, not a rule; price-sensitive categories and commodity products may behave differently.
Some buyers always chase the lowest price, so premium pricing depends on category and differentiation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use hidden listing attributes and a future offer start date for launch
cards.summary: Filling all attributes and setting a future offer start date lets you control launch timing and capture back-end discoverability fields.
cards.use_when: Finishing a new Amazon listing before hitting 'save and finish' and planning the launch day.
steps: Click 'all attributes' to reveal hidden fields most new sellers miss; fill the ones relevant to your product for extra discoverability.
Set the offer start date to a specific future day so the listing doesn't go live the moment it's approved.
Coordinate a truthful launch announcement to interested customers once stock and the listing are ready; do not organize purchases to manipulate rank or reviews.
Measure actual conversion and contribution; launch sales do not guarantee an organic ranking increase.
Complete back-end keyword fields — the source calls this section 'gold' because it tells Amazon which searches to show you for.
caveats: The velocity-to-ranking 'snowball' is the presenter's model, not a guaranteed algorithm behaviour.
Requesting incentivized/friend purchases may conflict with Amazon's review and manipulation policies — check current rules before acting.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Read Seller Central's home and inventory signals for restock timing
cards.summary: Daily Seller Central metrics (restock days-left, recommended quantity, buy box, open orders) drive replenishment decisions.
cards.use_when: Managing day-to-day operations and deciding when to reorder and ship replenishment inventory.
steps: Check the Restock Inventory widget for days of supply remaining and Amazon's recommended send quantity; the source treats very low days-left as urgent.
Confirm your Buy Box win rate hovers near 100% for a unique private-label product (dips are an advanced issue).
Monitor open orders, today's sales, and buyer messages; unanswered buyer messages can cost you points, so respond promptly.
Under Manage FBA Inventory, distinguish available vs inbound vs unfulfillable (damaged) vs reserved units. 'Reserved' typically means sold-but-not-yet-shipped or being transferred between warehouses.
Use this to trigger replenishment before stockouts, since the source warns running out is a common costly mistake.
caveats: Widget layout and field names in Seller Central change — verify the current interface.
Buy Box dynamics apply mainly to shared listings; unique private-label products rarely lose it.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Diagnose performance with Business Reports: sales, page views, conversion
cards.summary: Use Business Reports (sales & traffic) to separate traffic changes from conversion changes over time.
cards.use_when: Reviewing weekly or monthly store performance to decide whether to work on traffic or on conversion.
steps: Open Business Reports → Sales and Traffic; view by week or month for stable trends rather than noisy daily numbers.
Track total sales alongside total page views: the source's example saw page views roughly double (≈2,000 → ≈4,000 in a week) while conversion dipped slightly.
Read Unit Session Percentage as your listing conversion rate — the share of visitors who purchase.
Compare current month to last month and to same month last year (the report plots prior periods as overlays).
When traffic rises but conversion falls and total sales still grow, you may have a traffic win with a conversion nuance to investigate rather than a failure.
Use the findings to decide where to intervene: creative/ads for traffic, PDP/price/reviews for conversion.
caveats: Convert conversion metrics only for purchase conversion — this is listing conversion, not close rate or lead conversion.
Report periods and metric names change; verify current Seller Central labels.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Protect account health and address negative reviews
cards.summary: Monitor account-health issues separately from product reviews and resolve customer problems through permitted channels.
cards.use_when: Routine account maintenance and when a negative review or defect claim appears.
steps: Review current Account Health metrics, notices and required actions.
Investigate seller feedback, claims and chargebacks using the order evidence.
Use permitted support tools to resolve legitimate customer issues; do not seek reviewer identity outside approved tools or ask for a review change.
Treat product reviews as product-feedback data, not as interchangeable with seller feedback or account-health metrics.
Correct recurring listing, fulfillment or product problems and document the response.
caveats: Use current marketplace thresholds and communication rules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Activate Brand Referral Bonus to offset fees on off-Amazon traffic
cards.summary: Brand Registry sellers earn back roughly 10% of sales driven from external traffic to their Amazon listing.
cards.use_when: Running off-Amazon ads, influencer posts, or email campaigns that send buyers to your Amazon listing.
steps: Enroll in Brand Referral Bonus under the Brands dashboard (requires Brand Registry).
Point off-Amazon traffic to your Amazon listing using the tracked links so Amazon attributes the sale.
Treat the bonus as partial fee offset: the source cites an average ≈10% back, e.g. $5 on a $50 item, which helps cover FBA fees.
Cross-check against your ad spend — the bonus alone is small, so use it to improve ROI on external campaigns, not as a standalone profit source.
caveats: Requires Brand Registry and enrollment; bonus rates and terms can change — verify current programme details.
Only qualifying externally-referred sales count.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Create a case-pack template with correct box dimensions and weight
cards.summary: Before shipping to FBA, define a reusable case-pack template meeting Amazon's size/weight limits.
cards.use_when: Preparing the first FBA shipment or changing how you pack units into cases.
steps: From Manage Inventory, use 'Send/Replenish Inventory' on the product; if the option is missing, switch the item from FBM to FBA first.
Create a new case-pack template — a case is a container holding multiple units (e.g. ~40–45 tubs per box).
Ensure no side of the case exceeds 25 inches and the packed case weighs no more than 50 lbs (the source's box was 11x18x10 in at 37.35 lbs; the 45-unit example was 37.35 lbs).
Enter units per box and box dimensions; set prep category if your product needs special prep (adult, baby, fragile glass, liquids).
Save the template so repeat shipments reuse the same dimensions and unit count.
If you need boxes, buy locally or from a discounter like Uline.
caveats: Amazon's size/weight limits and prep requirements can change — verify current FBA shipping requirements.
Entering wrong dimensions causes fees and shipment problems.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Label units with FNSKU yourself or via manufacturer, not Amazon
cards.summary: Apply FNSKU labels before shipping; having Amazon label costs about $0.50/unit and is avoidable.
cards.use_when: Preparing units for an FBA shipment, especially private-label or wholesale/arbitrage products.
steps: Understand the difference: a UPC identifies the product for retail scanning, while an FNSKU identifies *your* specific inventory so Amazon can track which units are yours.
For private-label products, print the FNSKU directly on the packaging at the manufacturer — this avoids sticker costs and labor.
For retail arbitrage/wholesale, print FNSKU labels (via Seller Central 'print FNSKU labels') and stick them over the UPC barcode.
Buy sticker paper or ask your manufacturer to print and apply the labels for a small fee.
Avoid Amazon's labelling service (about $0.50/unit) whenever possible.
caveats: Regulations and label requirements vary by product/category — verify current Amazon FBA labelling rules.
Mislabeling causes receiving delays and lost inventory.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choose small parcel vs less-than-truckload by shipment size
cards.summary: Match the FBA shipping method to volume — small parcel for boxes, LTL/pallet for large shipments — to cut freight cost.
cards.use_when: Selecting a shipping method and carrier when creating an FBA shipment.
steps: For small volumes, choose small parcel delivery and ship via UPS, either dropping off or scheduling a pickup (the source shipped 9 cases, 336 lbs, for about $266).
For large volumes, switch to less-than-truckload and send full pallets — the source says this can roughly halve shipping cost versus repeated small-parcel sends.
If using LTL, confirm your manufacturer will accept a truck, can palletize, and wrap the load properly; you can also schedule a liftgate pickup from your home.
Use Amazon's discounted UPS rates where possible; choosing another carrier (DHL, FedEx, USPS) usually costs more.
Choose the correct marketplace destination and set the fulfillment capability appropriately (standard FBA vs multi-channel/blank-box if you also ship for your own website).
caveats: LTL requires a local trucking company, not UPS, and different paperwork (BOL).
Rates, pickup rules, and interfaces change — verify current options in Seller Central.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Double-check box labels: weight, dimensions, and addresses
cards.summary: Errors on shipment labels cause lost inventory, fees, and carrier surcharges — verify before dispatch.
cards.use_when: After generating FBA box labels and before handing packages to the carrier.
steps: Attach both labels to each box: the UPS/carrier label (for tracking) and the Amazon FBA box-ID label (which Amazon scans to track inventory at every move).
Keep the Amazon box-ID barcode untaped/uncovered — covering it can cause scan failures, lost inventory, or rejection.
Verify weight and dimensions for each case match what's declared; incorrect info can trigger UPS surcharges.
Confirm ship-from and ship-to addresses are correct, and that the ship-to on both labels matches — Amazon may route boxes to different fulfilment centres across the network.
Match the number of printed label pages to the number of boxes (e.g. 9 pages = 9 cases).
Print on sticker paper, or on plain paper and tape on carefully.
caveats: Addresses and routing can change per shipment; re-verify every time.
Label requirements and surcharge rules change — confirm current limits.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Track FBA shipments and reclaim lost inventory with documentation
cards.summary: Monitor shipment statuses and keep all paperwork to recover the value of lost or mis-received units.
cards.use_when: After sending inventory, while it's in transit and being received, and if quantities don't match.
steps: In Inventory → Manage FBA Shipments, monitor each shipment's status: in transit → delivered → receiving → closed. 'Delivered' only means the carrier dropped it off — no one has checked it in yet.
Expect Amazon to check-in within days to weeks after delivery; the source saw a shipment received Jan 28 but not cleared until Feb 25.
Under the Contents/Problems tabs, compare units shipped vs units received; a discrepancy (e.g. 405 sent, 400 received) is where you must prove what you sent.
Keep every receipt and document: BOL (bill of lading) for LTL pickups, truck pickup receipts, and case-pack records. Without proof, Amazon may not pay for missing units.
If evidence is sufficient, Amazon can pay you as though missing units were sold. The source lost a pallet's receipt and risked $10,000 until Amazon found the pallet months later.
To reduce risk, consider splitting a large send into two shipments a few days apart so a loss only affects half.
caveats: Amazon is not obligated to pay without adequate proof; recovery can take months.
Check-in, receiving, and claim timelines and interfaces change — verify current procedures.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Ship inventory 3–6 weeks ahead and avoid stockouts
cards.summary: FBA check-in can lag weeks, so plan replenishment with a buffer and never assume urgency speeds it up.
cards.use_when: Planning replenishment timing and launch timing for FBA products.
steps: Ship inventory at least 3 weeks before you expect it checked in; allow up to about 6 weeks, and expect longer during holidays.
Don't wait until you have only a week or two of stock — Amazon won't prioritize your shipment just because you'll soon be out of stock.
Use the Restock Inventory widget's days-left and recommended send quantity as an early trigger.
Separate receiving time from available-to-sell time: a shipment may sit 'delivered' but not 'receiving' for weeks.
For launch, schedule products to arrive and be checked in before your planned offer-start launch date.
caveats: The 3–6 week window is the presenter's rule-of-thumb, not a platform SLA.
Delays vary by season and warehouse load; verify current expectations.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx
